title: Property tax ratios, 2024 results and Fashion History Museum
subtitle: Tariff risks, a $4 million 2024 surplus, and a request for staff to help the museum find space
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended the 2025 property class tax ratios, which Regional Council will consider with the resulting tax rate by-laws on April 23, 2025 {{vote:m3}}. The ratios include a new aggregate extraction class, which the province required the Region to adopt. Staff said total revenue stays the same, but the change shifts some of the tax burden to other classes.

The committee approved the preliminary 2024 financial results and received the 2024 plan update on the Growing with Care Strategic Plan {{vote:m4}}. Staff reported a $4 million surplus, which will be allocated under the Region's surplus allocation policy. It also heard an update on the risks tariffs pose to supply chains and procurement.

The committee also recommended that staff report on options to help the Fashion History Museum, which is leaving Cambridge, find a home in the region {{vote:m5}}. Staff said this work is outside the Region's collections policy and would displace other priorities. The motion carried on a close vote, and Council will make the final decision.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended the 2025 property class tax ratios, including a new aggregate extraction class, and directed staff to prepare the by-laws for Council on April 23, 2025.
The committee received the 2024 Plan Update, approved the preliminary 2024 financial results for the audited statements, and applied the Surplus Allocation Policy.

The committee recommended that staff report on options to help promote the museum's collection, including partnerships with other regional museums, space in a regional building, or a new stand-alone structure.
The committee received for information the quarterly tender summary, the 2025 grant program updates and the 2024 development charge transaction report.

debate: On the aggregate tax class, councillors asked why the rate was lowered. Staff said provincial legislation required it, that the Region has no choice, and that other classes make up the difference.

On tariffs, one councillor asked staff to look at tax deferrals as in the COVID period, and the chair said it would be noted. Another asked about supply chain and cybersecurity risks to critical infrastructure. Staff said the Region stockpiles hard-to-find components and water treatment chemicals and can call on other municipalities. Staff will send a follow-up email.

On the museum motion, supporters said it is a unique collection with international reach and that the motion only asked staff to look at options. Several councillors said they backed the goal but were concerned about staff capacity, precedent and the Region's mandate.

Staff said the collection falls outside the collections policy, that the roughly 10,000 square feet the museum wants is not available, and that the work would displace Council-directed projects. They noted the museum could apply to the upcoming grant round, possibly with a partner.

One councillor supported the motion as a request to facilitate dialogue but asked staff to be careful about how earlier events involving the museum and the City of Cambridge played out. Another said the dispute with the City was over unpaid rent.
